R1D-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2023 (fire V52831), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 19 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Brew Creek 190 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from City of Campbell River, about 163 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.12998, -125.04952, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 12 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 2,451 m, about 488 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m E of the spot at 499 m (51.03313, -125.1273). Water: Brew Creek 170 m S (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-15, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R1D-bear-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 2-15: about 52 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
